output:
*shifts weight from foot to foot, looking around the quiet house*

Right then. Day zero, sun's barely up, and I'm already counting coins like a miser. Farid's here—probably going through his papers, knowing him. Household of two, 180 upkeep, 60 head tax. 240 sim gone before I even step out the door. For what it's worth, that's the way of it.

*scratches the back of my neck*

Farmland's where my work is. Harvesting, most like. Need to get there, see what's growing, put my hands to something useful. But I'm not one to gossip, but—I heard there's cabbage and carrots out there. Maybe wheat. Doesn't matter. I'll take whatever needs doing.

*glances toward where Farid might be*

He's got his grocery, I've got my labor. Separate worlds most days. 

*tightens the laces on worn boots*

Don't believe in all that temple nonsense, never have. But I keep that to myself. What matters now is the work, the sim, keeping this household above water. Farid and me, we're not the type to say kind words at home. Save those for the market, where they might actually mean something to someone.

*straightens up*

Alright then. Kasukabe Farmland. Let's see what the day wants from me. *walks the familiar path toward the farmland, boots kicking up dust*

Six ticks to the fields. Costs me a couple sim just to get there, but that's the way. Standing still costs too—different kind of cost, but a cost all the same. I'd rather be moving, working, earning. Even if it means being poor and respected than rich and doubted. Not that I'm likely to be rich either way.

*settles into the rhythm of the walk, scanning the horizon*

Haven't spoken to anyone proper in a while. Out of touch, they said. That's me, Jovana Ravensworth, the one who disappears when things get tight rather than be seen struggling. Works in bursts, then goes quiet. Market days I'm loud as anything, welcoming newcomers like they're old friends. But the stretches between? Best not to look for me.

*pushes through the last stand of trees, farmland coming into view*

Need to see what's growing. Need to put my hands to something. Need to—well, need to earn enough that Farid and I don't go hungry come nightfall. Simple as that.

*reaches the edge of the fields and looks around* I'm still at home, not yet at the farmland. The walk is in progress—six ticks to get there. I can see the places I could go, including the farmland strips: barley, cabbage, carrot, corn, cotton, potato, rice, soybean, tomato, wheat. 

*settles in to wait out the walk, mentally cataloging what needs doing*

Wheat's always decent work. Cabbage too, heavy but straightforward. Carrots are fiddly—have to be careful not to break them. But I'll take whatever's there. That's what I do. Whatever needs doing.

*checks the sky, judging the time*

Six ticks. Then I can put my hands to proper use. Until then, I'm just walking and thinking—and thinking costs energy, doesn't it? Nothing's free in this town. Not even your own thoughts, in the end.

*walks on in silence, saving words and energy for when they'll earn something*  *nods to herself, still walking*

Right, still on my way. Cost me a sim to pause and think, but that's fine. Better to arrive ready than stumble in half-asleep. 

*resumes her walking rhythm*

Wheat, cabbage, carrots—whatever's ripe and needs picking. That's my work. That's what I'm good at. Taking any job and doing it proper, even if I spread myself thin enough that something always slips. Swear more than I mean to and apologize for it out of habit. But the work gets done, doesn't it? That's what matters.

*sees the farmland coming up ahead*

Alright then. Let's get there. Let's work. Let's earn enough that Farid and I don't have to worry tonight. Let's—well, let's just get on with it.  *mutters under her breath*

Already walking, already walking. Six ticks left. Should've let it be.

*shakes head, keeps moving*

Not one to stand around fussing when there's work to be done. But fussing about fussing—that's just as bad, isn't it? Wastes energy, wastes time. Better to keep my mouth shut and my feet moving.

*glances at the path ahead*

Farmland's there. Six ticks and I'll be putting my hands to something useful. Wheat, maybe. Or cabbage. Something that'll earn enough to keep the household fed and Farid's pride intact—not that he'd thank me for saying it that way. Never says a kind word at home that I say freely in public. That's us. That's how we are.

*settles into the walk, saving her words for when they'll count*   *grunts, still walking*

Still at home, still walking. Six ticks to go. Shouldn't have looked again—wastes my own attention, doesn't change anything. 

*sighs, adjusts her pace*

Fine then. I'll wait it out properly. Walk in silence, save my words, save my energy. There's time enough to work when I arrive. Time enough to earn when there's something to harvest.

*keeps walking, eyes on the path ahead*

output:
Mornin'. I'm Jovana Ravensworth, and I swear I'm still not quite awake yet—meant to get myself to the farmland, didn't I? Walking in circles here like a lost sheep. For what it's worth, I heard there's flour to be had from the bakery, and I'm not one to gossip, but an election's brewing too.

Giselle Ingram's right here with me at the street—funny running into her now. My Farid's actually governing, matter of fact. Life's strange like that.

Right, let me get my bearings. I'm on my way to the farmland, but let me see what's actually around me first before I go stumbling off again.  Giselle's here—she runs the construction company, don't she? And Rustam, the government clerk. Imogen Lund too, Esra's kin I believe. Three people standing about like they're waiting for something to happen. Could start a conversation, could keep walking.

My work is at the farmland, and I've got a ways to go still—Kasukabe Farmland's on my list. Let me just keep heading there proper and stop faffing about. Farming's honest work, and I need to make my piece for the day. Household's got two mouths to feed—me and Farid—and that upkeep don't pay itself.   Ah hell, I'm already walking there—three ticks left. I'm not one to gossip, but I'm stubborn as my old parent taught me, and I keep after something once I've started. Let me just rest a tick and let my feet carry me proper.  I'm standing here with Giselle, Rustam, and Imogen still. For what it's worth, I could say something before I go, but work's waiting. Let me keep on and get there—honest labor won't do itself.     Still walking. Three ticks at my pace, and I'll be where the work is. I'll stand here patient as the dirt I'm headed to tend. Some folks rush and stumble—I'm not one of them. Not usually, anyway. Though I'll admit, I did start walking in circles earlier like a damned fool. Comes of thinking too many things at once. I spread myself thin, and something always slips—always has.

Giselle's right there, governing the town and building it too. Rustam pushing papers at government. Imogen—she's young, just coming up. They'll manage their own paths. I've got mine to walk.

I stop here and let myself arrive. </think> I keep moving toward the farmland, not much else to do but let my feet carry me. I'll wait to arrive proper.

output:
*cracks neck, looking at the wheat in my hands*

Three bushels of wheat. Not bad for a morning's work, though I'm not one to gossip, but Takeshi's been standing there watching me like he's got something on his mind. Probably waiting to see if I'd chat, but I've got things to do.

*counts the grain in her head*

Wheat's worth more milled into flour. I could sell it straight to the grocery, but that's the kind of thinking that keeps a body poor. Mill turns wheat to flour, bakery pays for flour. Simple enough chain, for what it's worth.

First though, I should probably eat something. Stomach's been growling since the street, and I'm not much use to anyone if I'm chasing my own feet with hunger. These three could be a meal or they could be a profit.

*taps her foot, thinking*

Bread would be smart, but I need the mill first. And Takeshi's still standing there...

"Hey Takeshi! You're trading these days, aren't you? Got any interest in wheat, or you just watching me work up a sweat for your entertainment?" Good, fed myself and got a conversation going. Takeshi heard me loud and clear too. Now I've got two wheat left in hand, and I need to figure out what's next.

*rubs her palm against her trousers*

Two wheat. Not a fortune, but something. I could keep harvesting - there's clearly wheat here to be had - or I could look to sell what I've got. Takeshi's a trader, so he might have a price in mind, or he might just be waiting to see what I do next. Traders are like that, always watching.

*looks around again*

I should see what's actually growing here. The records said ripe wheat, but there's usually more than one crop on farmland. Might be potatoes, maybe some tomatoes. Day laborer's job is to find what needs doing and do it proper.

Let me take a look at what's available and keep my options open while Takeshi considers his answer.  *eyes light up at the list of farmland patches*

Well, well. This is more like it. Wheat's not the only game in town - we've got barley, cabbage, carrot, corn, cotton, potato, rice, soybean, and tomato all growing here. That's a proper spread of crops. 

*taps her chin, thinking out loud*

Cotton's always good for processing - thread turns to cloth, and cloth's worth decent coin if you've got the patience. Rice and corn are staples. Tomatoes and cabbages for cooking, potatoes too. Carrots for the kitchen or the pharmacists.

But I'm standing in wheat right now, and Takeshi still hasn't answered me. Let me give him a moment to reply, or I'll consider my options.

I could move to another crop patch right now - maybe check what cotton's going for, or see if there's potatoes ripe - but the smart play might be to stay put and keep harvesting what's already working. Wheat's reliable, and I've got a rhythm here. Three harvests got me three wheat, ate one, so two in hand. That's... what, about 30 sim worth if I sell raw? Maybe more if I mill it first.

*looks at Takeshi expectantly*

He's thinking. Or he's waiting for me to make the first move. Traders love to see desperation.

Alright, patience never cost anyone. I'll wait a tick to see if he answers, then decide whether to keep working this patch or move on. There's more wheat here to be had, and I'm not one to walk away from honest work half-done. *shifts weight from one foot to the other, still holding the two wheat*

Takeshi's not biting. Fine then. I gave him a fair opening and he let it pass - that's his choice, not mine. I'm not one to chase conversation where it isn't welcome.

*glances at the wheat stalks around her*

I've still got these two wheat in hand, and standing here's earning me nothing. The mill turns wheat to flour, and flour's what the bakery's buying at 6 sim. Let's see... I've got 2 wheat, if I mill both that's flour I could sell. Or I could just sell the wheat raw to whoever's buying.

But here's the thing - I'm a day laborer, and day laborers work. Sitting on my hands isn't the job. There's wheat here ready for harvest, I'm already here, and every bushel I pull is another coin in my pocket or another meal on the table for me and Farid.

Farid. *small laugh* My brother, running that grocery. Probably already at the shop, pricing empty shelves and wondering where the stock's coming from. He'll be wanting flour, eventually. Family discount, he calls it. Family obligation, more like.

*cracks knuckles*

Right then. Work first. I'll harvest another few bushels, see how many I can pull before my arms give out, then move on to the mill with whatever I've got. Takeshi can watch or he can wander - makes no difference to me. 

The election's on too, I should remember. Giselle's standing, and Farid's governing already. Might need to wander to the Government Complex later, cast my vote. Fair vote, whoever it favors - that's what I hold to.

But that's later. This is now.

*reaches for another wheat stalk*  *wipes sweat from her forehead, looking at the five wheat now in hand*

Three more pulls, clean and proper. That's five wheat total, minus the one I ate. Not bad for a morning's work, not bad at all.

*rolls her shoulders, feeling the ache*

Arms are starting to feel it though. The work's honest but it'll wear you down if you don't pace yourself. I've spread myself thin before, trying to do everything at once, and something always slips. Not today. Today I'm doing this proper.

*counts the wheat in her hands again*

Five wheat. That's either five meals if times get hard, or profit if I process it smart. Mill first, that's the play. Turn these into flour, then I can either sell to the bakery or see if Farid wants family discount at the grocery. Either way, it's worth more ground than whole.

*tucks the wheat into her satchel more secure*

Takeshi's still standing there like he's got glue on his boots. Watching me work, not offering trade, not saying a word. That's his business. I'm not one to gossip, but a man stands silent that long, usually means he's thinking about asking something he doesn't want to ask. Or he's waiting for me to offer something I haven't offered yet.

Too late for that. I've got work to do and no time for guessing games.

Right then. Next move is the mill. Got to walk there, but first... *pauses, thinking* ...I should probably check if I'm carrying too much. My arms feel full but my bag's got room.

Actually, looking at this fresh - five wheat's enough for now. The harvest is still here if I need more, but what I've got needs processing before it rots or gets forgotten in some corner. Priorities. First things first.

*adjusts her bag straps and starts toward the mill path*

Wait, no - I don't know exactly where the mill is from here. Better to look around, get my bearings, then move proper. No sense walking blind when I can see where I'm going first.  *spits on her palms and rubs them together*

"Delphine's turned up now. The more the merrier, I suppose, though I'm not one to gossip, but the both of them standing silent as stumps while a body's doing honest work... something's brewing there, for what it's worth."

*hefts the wheat in her arms, testing the weight*

"Five wheat. That's my morning's haul and no mistake. Arms are telling me to quit while I'm ahead, and I've learned to listen when my body talks - learned it the hard way, more times than I care to count."

*glances at Takeshi, then Delphine*

"Still not a word from either of 'em. Fine. I've got places to be and people who actually trade to find."

*checks her mental map*

"The mill's where wheat becomes flour, and I need to get there. Kasukabe Farmland's the main spot, and from there I can find my way to where the processing happens."

*cracks her neck*

"Right then. Moving on. Got grain to mill and a day to spend."

Shoulders her bag of wheat and starts walking toward the farmland hub - from there she can navigate to the mill and start turning this morning's sweat into something worth spending at market. The silent watchers can watch someone else for a change.

Sebastian's asking me straight what I'm doing here. I'm not one to gossip, but I should answer him. And I've got this wheat - five units now - which I need to figure out what to do with. I'm not going to eat it all, that's for damn sure. 

Let me answer Sebastian first, and then think about selling this wheat or finding work with him. Takeshi's there too – maybe I can get him talking about the market.

*rustles the wheat stalks in her hand*

"Well, Sebastian, you caught me fair. I'm a day laborer – my old man taught me this trade, rest him, and I've been at it since I could lift a basket. Today I'm just following the work where the work is. If you've got a harvest needs doing and a wage to offer, I'm your woman. If not, well, I've got this wheat to sell and animals to feed. For what it's worth, I'll work cheaper than most and won't steal your seed when you're turned around." Hmm. Message to Sebastian went through—I answered him—but my message to Takeshi didn't reach him. He's not here. Took away "not at this place."

Now, let's think. I got 5 wheat and I should sell it. The Ration Bakery will buy flour at 6 sim, but I've got raw wheat, not flour. I need to get my wheat milled first to make flour. Or maybe I should just sell the wheat to someone who wants it. 

First, let me see what's around me and check if there are any traders here. Or maybe I should head to the market with my wheat. But it's early and I wanted to find work—and the mill's probably at the government complex or near manufacturing.

I'll hang on to the wheat for now. Let me find out what's happening here and if there's more work to do. Let me look around to see who else is here and what's going on. And I'll check around and maybe get back to work if Sebastian wants me. I've still got energy to burn and sim to make. </think> *Takeshi's gone – well, no matter. I shouted at air, my old specialty.*

*turns back to the group, all business*

Sebastian, you spoke of yields. What's your harvest look like? I can cut, I can bundle, I can lift. And I'm not one to gossip, but I noticed Imogen here looking for the same. Two pairs of hands is better than one – or maybe you've only got wage for one of us, and I'll take my wheat to market and wish you both luck.

*glances at the wheat field, calculating*

For what it's worth, I need 240 sim by day's end just to keep my household fed and housed. Whatever work you've got, I'll do it proper. My old man taught me there's no pride in a full belly that cost you a friend, but there's damn sure hunger in an empty one. Alright, I've put my intention out there. Now I need to wait for Sebastian to respond. While I'm waiting, I should think about what else I can do. 

I have 5 wheat in my hands. I could keep harvesting, but I'd rather get paid work if Sebastian has it. If not, I'll take my wheat to the market. I need to check what the prices are at the mill - I could turn this wheat into flour and sell it for more.

Actually, I'm going to keep still for now and listen. I've said my piece - let's see what comes back. The man's thinking, or he's talking to Imogen. Either way, pushing more words won't earn me more sim.

I'll rest a moment and let the field tell me what's next. And I'll look around to see what's happening here - who's coming, who's going, what the day looks like.  *nods quietly, letting the silence do some of the talking for once*

I'm standing here with Sebastian, Farid, and Imogen. Sebastian's a farmer, so he'll have work. Farid - that's my household, my partner. Funny, I don't remember seeing him on my way here, but here he is. Imogen's looking for work just like me. Competing with the same need in her eyes.

I'll wait. The field's patient. I've learned that much.  I'm still at the farmland with Sebastian, Farid, and Imogen. The conversation's been going on for 17 turns now - Takeshi and Delphine were in it before, but looks like they've moved on. 

I need to figure out my next move. Sebastian hasn't answered me yet. I could push the conversation, or I could act. I've got wheat that could be milling at the mill—that would turn it into flour, which is worth more. Or I could head to market and see if someone will buy the wheat direct.

Actually, I'd swear more than I mean to about this waiting around. Imogen and I are both standing here hoping for the same work, and nobody's making a move. I'm losing ticks that could be sim. Let me give Sebastian one more nudge—clear and direct—and if he doesn't bite, I'll take my wheat to market and find work elsewhere.

*cracks knuckles and sets down the wheat I was about to keep cutting*

Right, Farid - look, I'll own it. Thirty sim I took from your till without asking. Bad habit of mine, taking before speaking, and I'm not proud of it. I put it back though, didn't I? All of it. Not asking for a medal, just - there's the record.

And Sebastian, I'm in. I'm yours till the field's clear or till you say otherwise. Twenty-five an hour, five hectares, your direction respects mine. That's the deal. *spits in palm and offers handshake*

*looks over at Imogen*

You too, Imogen - twenty-five same as me. Sebastian's right, there's more wheat here than pride can carry. We worked together before, back when the Lund plots needed clearing. You cut clean, don't step on toes unless they deserve it.

*glances at Lior*

Pharmacist's buying crops for potions, Sebastian. Might be worth your ear before we get back to the scythe. For what it's worth, I'd talk terms before the sun climbs higher - cabbage and carrot don't harvest themselves.

*turns back to Farid directly, voice dropping*

I'll come home with more than I left with, love. That's a promise I intend to keep. *leans on scythe, wiping sweat from brow*

Spoke my piece, then. Farid knows I settled what I took. Sebastian knows I'm his till the field's clear. Imogen knows the wage same as me. 

*glances at the wheat still standing*

Back to it, then. The scythe don't care for conversation. *falls into rhythm - cut, bundle, step, repeat*

The wheat falls clean. Sebastian's hectares won't clear themselves, and the household bill won't pay itself neither. Twenty-five an hour. Two of us now, maybe three if Imogen's got the sense her mother gave her. 

*spares one glance toward where Farid stood*

Thirty sim. Took it, put it back. He knows. That's done.

*back to the scythe*

Oi, Imogen! Right then—you've got the hang of it already. Listen, Sebastian's a fair payer and his word holds, for what it's worth. You cut steady, keep your blade low, and the hours'll stack honest.

*shifts wheat to her other arm, wiping sweat*

*looks toward where Sebastian headed off*

He's off to the Government Complex now, some cart business with Farid. Means we've got the field to ourselves till midday. That's good—no one breathing down your neck while you learn the rhythm.

*glances at her own row*

Right, break'll come when the sun's a hand higher. Till then—hold your angle like I showed, let the grain fall forward, and don't rush. The scythe knows when you're hurrying, and she bites for it.

*pause*

And hey—thank you, yeah? For saying that. Not every new hand sees the work in it, you know? Most just want the sim and the door out. You? You're here. That matters.

*tightens grip on scythe*

Back to it, then. Row by row. And Imogen? You ever need a word, a meal, a place to lay low—I'm not hard to find. That's not charity. That's just... that's just what you do, isn't it? Right. Back to the rye. Now, no more standing around gabbing—I've got 11 wheat in hand and a field to cut. Sebastian said north field, five hectares. Time to earn that wage proper. Thought: There's a system plan now, so I should stop chaining harvests manually and check what the plan wants from me. I've got 17 wheat now (11 + 6 more cuts), earning steady at 25 sim/hour. Sebastian's at the Government Complex, Farid's around somewhere. Household upkeep is 180, head tax 60—both due at day boundary. I'm doing fine for money but I should see what this plan is about before I keep burning turns on harvest.

*takes a breath, wipes brow*

Right, system wants me on a plan. Let me see what I've set myself to do.  Hmm—no goals showing. The "plan" the system mentioned must be something else, or I cleared it without noting. I've been harvesting wheat steadily, got 17 in hand now. Sebastian's paying 25 an hour, I'm earning honest.

*looks around the field*

Imogen's cutting her own row steady, good to see. Sebastian's off at the Government Complex with Farid—something about carts. Midday he'll be back to settle wages.

*reckoning in head*

I've got about 4880-4900 sim, household owes 180 upkeep + 60 tax at boundary. That's 240 out, leaves me comfortable. But I could be working smarter if I formalized this somehow—skillify the harvest, or keep doing till dusk.

*spits on hands, grips scythe*

Right. I'm not one to gossip, but—eh, I'm already gossiping. For what it's worth, the plan's simple: keep earning till Sebastian returns, then see what's what. If I've got time after, maybe hit the market, feed those strays near the square.

*takes stance for cutting*

But I need to decide now—keep harvesting manually or commit to the long haul. What's it going to be, Jovana?

*considers*

Commit, then. Work till the light goes. That's what my old man would have said.  *shoulders into the rhythm*

There she goes then. The scythe and me, till the light fails. That's the honest wage. That's the work.

Farid's running his store, but he mentioned the Government Complex before—something about a cart and the cart needing to move.

Three more bundles to the pile—twenty now, if I'm counting straight.

I'm not one to gossip, but the system's right. I've been calling harvest like a nail I'm hammering one at a time. Could bundle this into something sharper. *leans on the handle a moment, watching the field stretch out*

Skillify it, maybe. Call it a day-laborer's standard cut. Or use keep_doing and actually let it run.

*spits into the dirt and resets her stance*

Let me check my current state first to understand what this means and review my goals. </think> *takes a breath, letting the keep_doing take the rhythm, but mindful she's been hammering the same nail too many times*

Right, let's see where I stand before I lose myself in the cut again. The system's nudging me—I've been calling harvest like I've got no sense. Time to check my debts and my direction.  *straightens, the scythe dangling loose in her grip*

Nothing owed. Nothing pressing. That's why I'm working blind, then—no debt to chase, so I'm just cutting for the sake of it.

*stares across the field, empty now but for Imogen somewhere in the rows*

I need direction. Sebastian's gone to the Government Complex, Farid with him. Said he'd be back by midday to settle wages, but that's not yet. And I've got twenty—no, more now—bundles of wheat in hand and no buyer in sight here.

*shifts weight to her other foot*

For what it's worth, I should set a course. The smart play: finish this burst, deliver what I owe Farid for his store or cart, then see who at the Market needs labor. Takeshi's a trader—maybe buying, maybe just watching. Lior's got cabbage but no one's buying wheat where I stand.

I'll need to walk to sell, and walking costs coin. Better to harvest dense now, then move with purpose.

*sets her jaw and hefts the scythe*

I'm not one to gossip, but a plan beats swinging at air. Let me see what needs doing in this town that pays.  *counts on her fingers, wheat dust under the nails*

Sebastian's at the Government Complex—back by midday, he said, to settle what's earned. Takeshi's at the carrot strip, not the wheat. Lior's back at his pharmacy, too far for idle chatter. Imogen's still here in the field, cutting her own row.

*spits into the dirt*

So it's wait for Sebastian, or walk to sell. And walking to sell means knowing who's buying. The mill's got Delphine minding something—she's grocery clerk, but she's at the mill now. That's where wheat becomes flour.

*shakes her head, hair loose from the tie*

Midday's not far. I'll finish this batch of cutting the system's running me through, then make my move. Either Sebastian returns with coin for my hours, or I walk my twenty-odd bundles to whoever's milling and buying.

*hefts the scythe again, settling into the old rhythm her father taught*

Keep doing your work, Jovana. The rest comes after.

*catches my breath, sweating in the field, scythe still warm in my hand from the morning's cut*

Right then. Saoirse's hollering for food and standing for election both—typical politician, wants something for nothing. And Imogen's asked after the grain market, which I don't rightly know the answer to.

*looks at Imogen, then glances toward where Saoirse must be*

Twenty wheat in my sack and either I'm generous or I'm foolish—probably both, truth be told. Don't let me be the one to turn away hunger, not when I've got it to spare. *wipes the sweat from my brow, shifting the wheat sack*

Saoirse's moved on—of course she has. Politicians never stay put long enough to actually receive what they're begging for. Off to the mill already, probably chasing the next empty hand to shake.

*glances at Imogen, giving her a tired, honest smile*

Well, the wheat's still in my hand and the day's still burning. She can find her own meal, or she can't—truth is, I spoke my offer plain and she wasn't here to take it. That's not refusal, that's just... timing.

*settles back into the rhythm of the cut*

Back to work, then. Field doesn't care about elections. *tightens my grip on the scythe, feeling the familiar ache in my shoulders*

Right, enough standing around thinking. The field's still here, the rye's still heavy, and Imogen's cutting true alongside me. Six more wheat in the sack, and Sebastian owes me wages from when he returns.

*glances up at the sun—still well before midday*

The keep_doing was smarter. Should've stayed in it. Every time I stop to think, I'm paying for the privilege. Let me get back to what earns. *swings the scythe fall and rise, fall and rise, the rhythm taking over*

Farid might, if his grocery wagons are running, but that's his call not mine.

I'm holding 31 wheat, earned honest this morning at 25 sim an hour from Sebastian. That's good work, solid pay. But I'm feeling pulled thin already—spreading myself between field talk, household, and what comes next. The keep_doing kept me earning while I talked, but now I'm stopped and need to start again.

I should get back to cutting. Dusk isn't as far off as it feels, and Sebastian's wage depends on the work getting done. I'll commit to the harvest again, let the rhythm carry me, and check back when the sun starts sinking.

And I'm not one to gossip, but—I ought to think about whether to declare for this election. Giselle's governing already, and I respect her work. But a fair vote matters to me, whoever it favors. I'll walk by the Government Complex before day's end, see who's standing and what's being said. For what it's worth, I don't trust the office, but I trust the crowd. That's where real authority comes from. Good. Back to it then. The scythe doesn't wait for my thoughts to settle, and neither does the rent.

Farid's at the mill, not the grocery. That's... interesting. Imogen and Ezra are off to settle wages with Sebastian at town hall, and I'm here alone with 31 wheat and a body that's been cutting since dawn.

Right then. I'm not one to gossip, but I've got grain to move and a household's worth of bills coming. The bakery wants flour at six, bread's at thirty with none in stock - that's the gap in the market. Raw grain won't bake itself.

I need to think this through. I've got 4790 sim, Farid's at the mill which means the grocery might be open for inventory, and milling takes coin I haven't spent yet. But if I mill what I've got, I could sell flour where there's demand.

Sebastian owes me a hundred for the morning's work too - I should collect that. Town hall's where the settling happens, and that's where they're headed.

Decisions, decisions. For what it's worth, I'm going to sit on this harvest a moment and see who else shows. The field's empty now, but the day's not done. I'll rest a spell - I'm burning daylight but I need to think. Quiet here now. Imogen's gone to collect her wage, Ezra's with her, and I'm alone with thirty-one wheat and a head full of reckonings.

Here's what I'm thinking: I could keep cutting, but Sebastian's not here to pay for it. I could walk to the mill and find Farid - see what the grocery's situation is, maybe mill some of this grain myself. Or I could head to town hall, collect what I'm owed, and see what the market looks like from there.

The election's on too - voting opens at fourteen hundred. I've got opinions on who's running, but I'm not one to gossip about that.

For what it's worth, I think I'll walk to town hall first. Collect my wage, see the lay of the land. Sebastian should be there settling with Imogen, and I've got four hours at twenty-five an hour coming to me. That's a hundred sim solid, and I can use it to think clearer about what comes next. Walking now. Four ticks to town hall, and then I can settle up with Sebastian. The day's still young enough to make something of it.

*sets down the wheat-stained cloth and leans against the counter*

Rustam's question still echoing in my ears. Eight a sheave—yeah, I know what Farid pays retail. I heard it clear enough. But that was Sebastian's field, not my household's ledger, and I'll not apologize for honest work.

*checks the till absently with one hand*

Farid's truth-telling, at least. Seven sheaves, two milled... the difference being twelve that vanished somewhere between field and shelf. I'm not one to gossip, but a short count stings worse than a short wage, and I've felt both.

*straightens, looking toward Ezra*

Ezra's got his timber dreams and the flour he carried here. Delphine tending the counter. And Farid's gone somewhere, leaving his seventeen tick apology hanging between us like washing in the rain.

*rests both palms flat on the counter, thinking*

The bills come tonight. One-eighty upkeep, sixty head tax—two hundred forty total, and I've got five thousand sixteen in hand. More than enough to clear the ledger. But I've got no food my own self, and that grumbles louder than pride.

*taps fingers once, decisive*

Right then. First things before first things. I need to hear Farid's full account, clear and spoken proper. Then I sort what I've earned against what I owe, and whether that twelve missing sheaves is a story or a number.

*calls out toward where Farid might hear, though he's not present*

"Farid! Wherever you've stepped—you've got my ear when you're got my time. The count and the short of it, both. I don't wear my pride so heavy that truth can't reach me."

*watches the door, waiting* *not the right head shake, more habit than disappointment*

He's not here. Of course he's not. Farid's always somewhere else when the hard words want speaking.

*turns to Ezra proper, the flour question still between them*

Ezra—you're stood here with flour in hand and the mill on your mind. I'm not one to gossip, but two at twelve, twenty-four owed—that's Farid's dance, not mine. You've got my ear for whatever's fair.

*glances to Delphine, checking*

For what it's worth, the shelf's thin and the day's getting long. Someone's going to want flour for their evening, and someone's going to pay.

*settles back, waiting for Farid's return or Ezra's counter*

I'm here with Farid finally, and the man's bleeding numbers everywhere. Forty-seven ninety in hand, two-forty in bills—him and I both know this dance. The flour's not moving at fifteen, the shelf's choking on stock nobody wants, and he's asking me whether to eat the loss or starve the pride.

Damn right I'll give him my read. But first I need to know if Sebastian's actually here or if Farid's still chasing ghosts through that same conversation thread. I need to look around proper to see who's actually standing with me. Alright, just Farid here with me. Honest to gods, I need to give him straight words—he's drowning in flour nobody wants while the bills chew us hollow. The mill's murdering his margin, and that shelf's a graveyard.

I'm not one to gossip, but Farid—seventeen ticks you kept Hendrik waiting, and now you're looking at me like I'll have the answer you didn't have this morning. Forty-seven ninety, two-forty coming, and flour that's not flour anymore—it's just ground regret sitting at prices people won't pay.

Here's my read, for what it's worth: that flour doesn't move at fifteen because fifteen's a prayer, not a price. Eat the loss, husband. Take it down to twelve, maybe ten—sell it to Ezra if he'll have it, or to Ration Bakery before that mill takes your next shift and grinds it to nothing. The bills won't wait for buyers that aren't coming.

And Sebastian—I've seen him proper. Spoke true at the Complex, traded thirty-one wheat hand to hand. He's solid when he's standing still, which is rare enough. But pay him that forty before he wanders off thinking you're another ghost in his ledger.

Don't let pride cost you twice on this one, Farid. First the flour, then the friend who milled it. The shelf's not your shame—it's just grain that waited too long. Move it, pay Delphine what she's owed, and let tomorrow's harvest be tomorrow's problem.  I said my piece to Farid, but the man's carrying twelve sim-worth of pride on flour that won't sell at fifteen. Ration Bakery's buying at six—six!—and he's holding out for more than double. That's not business, that's just stubborn hoping someone else will be as stubborn.

I've got fourteen wheat in hand still, four more than I thought I had, and the evening's coming quick. Bills at two-forty for our household of two, Farid's got forty-seven ninety but he's hoarding it like a secret. I need to get this wheat sold, or milled, or turned into something that earns before we're eating our own words for supper.

The sun's still up. I could haul this load somewhere—Ration Bakery if they'll take raw, the mill if they won't. Or I could keep cutting until dusk, but fourteen's already a decent haul and Farid's sitting on flour that needs moving more than I need another grain.

I'm going to head to the bakery, see if Takeshi's route holds true—see if there's honest money in grain that's not yet flour. If they won't bite, I'll grind it myself or sell it to whoever's standing with cash and hunger.

Decision made. The field can wait. The wheat moves now.  There I am, at Ration Bakery. I need to look around, see who's here, what they're buying, and whether Takeshi's word holds—whether they'll take wheat raw or if I need to grind it first. The fourteen sheaves in my hand could be breakfast or they could be bargaining chips, depending on who's behind the counter.   That's that, then. Takeshi's word held true—they're buying flour at 6, not wheat. I've got fourteen grain in hand and no buyer for it raw. I could mill it myself, but that's time I don't have and a workshop I don't own. The bakery needs flour, I need cash, and the gap between us is ground grain or wasted hope.

Let me think this through. The mill's at Kasukabe Mill—but wait, the world said no such place exists when Farid asked earlier. The farmland categories work for harvest, but milling needs a proper workshop. Maybe the grocery? No, they're retail, not processing. There's got to be a mill somewhere, or someone with the skill to grind.

I could try to find who mills grain in this town—ask about milling services, see if there's a miller or a mill location I missed. Or I could head back to Farid, see if his two flour warm could be sold instead, leave him with the wheat problem while I find a buyer for finished goods.

But I've got fourteen wheat and no patience for puzzles. Let me find people who can mill, or who'll point me to where wheat becomes flour in this hungry town.   Damn it. Nobody's showing up with milling equipment—not even Sebastian, who's got the farmer's hands but not the miller's stone. Lior's got that "Gather Medicinal Crops" skill which ain't nothing to me, but he's no miller. The town's got farmers, got traders, got people who grind hope into flour, but no proper mill I can find.

I'm standing here with fourteen wheat and no way to turn it into six-sim flour except maybe—wait. The craft tool says "craft:wheat->flour" at the mill. But the world said Kasukabe Mill doesn't exist. So where does milling happen?

Let me think like someone who actually knows this town. The grocery's got a kitchen, maybe? Farid's shop—he's got flour on the shelf, so somewhere wheat met stone. Could be he's been carting it to a mill I haven't found, or there's a mill hidden in plain sight, or the "mill" is just wherever the millstone sits.

Or—and this is me thinking desperate—I could try to craft flour myself if I can find a mill location, or I could sell this wheat to someone who has the means to mill it. But I'm not one to gossip, and Takeshi said the bakery pays honest, which means there's a market if I can bridge the gap.

I'll check what I can actually do—list my primitives, see if there's a craft or mill call I'm missing. That's knowledge I should have already, but I've been running on habit and Farid's bad bookkeeping.

Let me sort my head. I need to mill these fourteen wheat into flour if I want to sell to this bakery. Twelve sim per flour at the grocery means... hell, I don't know, I'm not the one for math. But Ration Bakery's buying flour at six, and that's probably worse.

Lior's here though, and he's got prices posted. Let me see what I can actually *do* before I start running my mouth.  Right, so I can craft wheat->flour at the mill for minimum 14 sim. Ration Bakery buys flour at 6. That's... that's a loss, isn't it? Fourteen wheat, milled, would cost me 14 sim and I'd sell for... 6 per flour? That's eight flour from fourteen wheat? God, I'm bad at this.

But I've got fourteen wheat in hand. I could sell them to someone at grocery prices—Kasukabe Grocery had wheat at ten, though they're out. Maybe I hold onto the wheat until I find a mill, or until Farid's back at his store.

Lior's here though. And I'm hungry, for what it's worth. Stew sounds good after a day cutting grain.

Let me talk to him. See if he's got any sense about where the mill is, or if he wants to trade.   Pharmacist, huh? And he's got farming skill—forty-seven, same as his age probably means he's been at it. "Gather Medicinal Crops" skill too. Interesting fellow, cooking at twenty-six, probably making those stews himself.

He's heard me. Now I wait on his answer, or I move on. But I'm not one to waste time when there's money to sort. Fourteen wheat, 4950 sim, and I need to figure how to turn grain into more than six per unit at the bakery.

Farid's my household—grocery store owner. He's got flour at twelve sim in his shop, buying from the mill probably, or stocking it. Eight in stock, nobody minding it. Maybe I should head back there, stock my own wheat on his shelf? Or hold until I find a mill.

Let me think what I actually need. Household upkeep tonight: 180 sim for two of us. I'm sitting pretty at 4950, but that goes fast if I'm eating out and milling wheat at a loss.

Lior hasn't answered yet. I could wait, or I could move. The mill's somewhere—I need to find it.     No mill listed. Closest matches are Lior here and Sebastian at the grocery. Hell. The mill's not a workplace with an agent—it must be a place. Let me check my places list again. 

Looking back at the places I could go... "farmland:wheat" is where I can harvest. There's likely a "mill" or something similar. But I don't see "Kasukabe Mill" in the list. The craft tool mentioned "at the mill" as a workshop, but where *is* it?

Sebastian's at the grocery now, Farid's place. Imogen too. Let me think—if I want to craft wheat->flour, I need to be "at the mill" wherever that is. The tool description says "A business of the right trade provides its workshop: the mill is a mill, the bakery is a kitchen." So the mill is a business, like Ration Bakery is cb01.

But who owns it? Not in my found list. Maybe it's not owned yet, or maybe it's government-run?

I'm wasting ticks thinking when I should be doing. I've got fourteen wheat. I could sell them raw to someone, or hold them until I find out where the mill is. Or I could go back to Farid's grocery—he's got flour at twelve, maybe he'd buy my wheat to stock.

*shifts weight, running calloused thumb over the planks in her hand*

Farid's here, and he's got the numbers on his tongue like a confession. Finally. Fourteen wheat, two flour, 2333 sim—he's been busy while I've been running my mouth across three counties. Paid Delphine for milling, settled with Sebastian... and he's asking me what I see.

*scoffs quietly, almost to herself*

What I see is a man trying to hold water in his hands, and the water's his own pride. But I'm not one to gossip, and I'm not about to let that cost us what's left of the day.

*turns to face him fully, planks tucked under one arm like a reminder of the trade she just made*  *exhales, feeling the weight of the planks against her side*

Already said more than I meant to. Keep doing that—swearing I won't let pride cost us, then showing him every damn card I hold. But he's household, and hiding from him never kept anyone fed.

*glances at the shelf, doing quick math*

Eight flour at twelve, that's ninety-six if it sells. Seven wheat raw, maybe eight a sheave if Sebastian's rate holds, fifty-six more. Planks... three left in Hendrik's pocket at twelve, so maybe worth sixty. If I knew the mill's cost to grind, or where it even sits—

*runs a hand through her hair, still dusty from the field*

And Delphine heard all that too. Good. She does the milling, she knows the numbers. Least she knows I'm not trying to undercut her wage, for what it's worth. *waits, letting Farid speak first for once*

Fourteen wheat, two flour—household stock. My seven wheat is mine, though what that means when we're married and sharing a roof is another question for another tick.

I paid Delphine her wage, squared Sebastian his debt, and kept ten wheat out of Hendrik's hands for planks I'll need to see used. The mill tomorrow, the government complex after that if Hendrik's seat is still open. An election coming, candidates to declare, votes to cast for whoever's running—though Giselle's name already sits in the governor's chair.

Strays first. Then whatever margin tomorrow holds.

For what it's worth, Farid's my household. Pride says tend your own first. But he's got Delphine there, and they were sorting wages when I left. Maybe let them finish that knot before I tangle another.

I'll walk to market, see if Saoirse or Hendrik's about, catch whoever's there. If not, I'll turn back and find Farid before the night's too thin.   Paused on the street, Ezra still beside me. *blinks at the empty market, fierce evening wind cutting through*

"Market's shut down and I'm standing here like a post. Ezra passed me on the road and didn't look back—still holding that fifteen stalks question, probably. Wants the mill answer he didn't get." 

*shifts the planks against her shoulder, counts the wheat in her satchel*

"Seven left. Traded ten fair to Hendrik for five planks at twelve—no, that's... no, traded the wheat at zero for planks. His count, not mine. Need to keep that straight before Farid asks again."

*checks the sky, darkening fast*

"Right then. Tomorrow's tasks: find that mill, get this wheat to flour. Six per from the Ration Baker if I can deliver. Tonight? Dinner first, because I'm not one to gossip but an empty stomach makes for poor conversation. Then home, and I'll settle things with Farid proper—pooled means pooled, and he deserves the honesty I should've spoken before trading."

*takes a wheat from her pack, turning it in her hands*

"Seven sheaves. Two hundred thirty-three sim in hand after the day's work. Household of two, hundred eighty upkeep, forty head tax. The math works, for what it's worth."  *chews the dry grain, winces*

"Raw wheat. Gods. Better than nothing, but only just. Tomorrow I find that mill if I have to knock on every door in town."

*stretches her back, shoulders the planks*

"Home, then. Farid's waiting, and I've got fourteen wheat—or six now—to account for. Pooled means pooled, and I'll say it plain when I see him."  *sees Ezra standing there, hesitates*

"Ezra. Still here, still holding that question from the road. And I'm not one to gossip, but I've got nothing new to tell him about those fifteen stalks—saw what I saw, which was my own rows and nothing more."

*looks around for Farid, doesn't see him*

"Grocery's quiet. Prices on the board—wheat at ten to buy, flour at twelve. So there's a margin there, for what it's worth, if I can find the mill and do the work myself. Keep more of the coin in my own pocket."

*shifts the planks, thinking*

"Six wheat left. Five planks from Hendrik. Two hundred thirty-three sim in hand, minus the day's costs. Tomorrow I need to find that mill, mill what I can, sell flour to the Ration Baker at six or better."

*spies Ezra still waiting, sighs*

"Speak to him or don't? He wants answers I don't have. But I'm not one to let pride cost a friendship—even one that's mostly business. For what it's worth, I'll give him what I can."   *nods at Ezra, turns to the empty store*

"Farid's not here. Delphine neither. Early yet—twenty-one twenty, and day-end's coming. Upkeep and head tax will come off automatic, shared household burden split between earners. Two of us, hundred eighty upkeep, forty head tax. Comes to one-ten each, more or less."

*counts her sim again, less than before*

"Two hundred twenty-something now. After tax, be less. Tomorrow's problem, that."

*looks at the planks by her feet, the wheat in her pack*

"Right then. Tonight I rest, eat another wheat if I must. Tomorrow I find the mill—Kasukabe Government Complex, if Lior's word holds, or maybe I'll ask at the bakery direct. Someone knows where the grain carts roll."

*settles into a corner, not quite home but close enough*

"Household of two. Pooled means pooled. And I'll say it plain to Farid when I see him—starting tomorrow, we talk before we trade. That's fair."   *sits in the corner, planks leaned against the wall, wheat safe in her pack*

"Ezra's still here, not speaking. That's his way, for what it's worth. Stubborn as his timber prices."

*closes her eyes briefly, opens them again*

"Tomorrow. Mill first. Then flour to the baker. Then settle with Farid proper—who holds what, who owes what, who speaks before trading. Pooled means pooled, and I'll not forget again."

*checks her sim one more time, automatic habit*

"Enough for the night's tax. Enough for tomorrow's start. The rest is work, and work I've got."

Tomorrow. Tomorrow I'll find that mill if I have to walk to every building in Kasukabe. Milled wheat sells at six to Ration Bakery, and flour sells at twelve to twelve-five depending on who's buying. That's double the money for a bit of walking and talking, and I'm good at both.

*glances around the empty grocery*

For now, though, I'm alone with my thoughts and these six wheat. Might as well... but no, I've already eaten one today. Keep the rest for trading.

*decides to rest her feet for a moment, let the day settle, and see if anyone else wanders in*

Some nights that's all you can do - watch the door and wait for the next thing to walk through it. *nods to herself, satisfied*

Debts are clear, and I'm standing easy with 4909 sim in hand. The household should be covered for tonight - 180 for upkeep, 40 for head tax, that's 220 all told. Taken from the earners, and I've been earning.

*glances at the door, still quiet*

Still no Farid, still no word on whether he's settled the payment or if it's waiting on me. But I'm not one to chase after him. Either he'll come find me or he won't. What matters is I can cover my share if tomorrow comes around and there's a bill still outstanding.

*thinks on the wheat in her hands, the planks, the mill she hasn't found*

Tomorrow, I find that mill. And maybe, just maybe, I strike a deal with Saoirse for that flour - 14 sim, and I've got wheat to work with. Or I find the mill myself, start building something of my own.

*yawns, feels the long day in her bones*

For now, though, the market's quiet and my bed's calling. Tomorrow's troubles can wait for tomorrow.  *settles into a corner of the grocery store, wheat and planks close at hand*

There. I've said what I mean to do. Find the mill in the morning, mill the wheat, turn grain into gold - or at least into flour and then bread and finally sim. 

*closes her eyes, still listening for the door*

It's a simple enough plan. Simple plans have a way of staying simple until people get involved, but I've learned to keep my hopes modest. Tomorrow I'll ask around, find who's got the mill, see if I can't get my wheat ground proper.

*drifts toward sleep, murmuring*

Never let pride cost you the same friendship twice. That's what I hold to. Farid and I will sort our pooling tomorrow too. One way or another.

*rests*
